1. Which histological type of bladder cancer is the most common?
a. Urothelial carcinoma
b. Squamous cell carcinoma
c. Adenocarcinoma
d. Mesothelioma
e. Small cell carcinoma
row.Reference: Strojan, P., & Hočevar, M. (Eds.). (2018). Onkologija: Učbenik za študente medicine [Oncology: Textbook for medical students] (1st ed.). Onkološki inštitut Ljubljana.
row.Context: The most common histological type is urothelial (transitional cell) carcinoma (over 90%), with squamous cell carcinoma (6–8%) and adenocarcinoma (2%) being less frequent. Urothelial carcinomas are classified by degree of differentiation according to two systems, both of which are in use. According to the WHO 1973 classification, they are divided into: G1 – well differentiated, G2 – moderately differentiated, G3 – poorly differentiated. According to the WHO 1998 classification, they are divided into: papillary urothelial neoplasm of low malignant potential, low-grade urothelial carcinoma, high-grade urothelial carcinoma.

a. Ovarian cancer
b. Cervical cancer
c. Lung cancer
d. Breast cancer
e. Endometrial cancer
row.Reference: Strojan, P., & Hočevar, M. (Eds.). (2018). Onkologija: Učbenik za študente medicine [Oncology: Textbook for medical students] (1st ed.). Onkološki inštitut Ljubljana.
row.Context: Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women in the developed world, accounting for the leading cancer in 140 out of 184 countries, making it an important public health issue. The estimate for 2012 was 1.7 million new cases worldwide. The risk of breast cancer generally depends on the country’s level of development, with rates decreasing from north to south and from west to east in Europe. In 2012, the incidence rate of breast cancer in Belgium was 148/100,000, in Denmark 143/100,000, and in Slovenia, for the period 2008–2012, it was 117/100,000 inhabitants. In Slovenia, the incidence also decreases from west to east across the country. For 2015, it was estimated that 1,287 new cases of breast cancer would be detected.

row.Context:
Hidden blood in stool can be an early sign of potentially serious changes in the colon and rectum. Numerous studies have shown that regular stool screening between the ages of 50–74, followed by colonoscopy and treatment of any detected lesions in those with positive results, reduces mortality from this cancer.
The SVIT program, led and coordinated by the National Institute of Public Health, is organized in accordance with European guidelines for quality assurance in colorectal cancer screening. Every two years, men and women aged 50–74 are invited to participate by taking two stool samples at home and sending them by mail to the central laboratory of the SVIT program. There, they perform an immunochemical test for hidden blood. All those with positive results undergo colonoscopy and, if needed, are directed to treatment.

These are usually slow-growing tumors in light-skinned populations that rarely metastasize, yet they still cause significant morbidity. They grow in a locally destructive manner and often recur, which can leave undesirable cosmetic consequences.

b. Radiation-induced fibrosis
c. Radiation-induced second malignancy
d. Acute radiation dermatitis

row.Context:
Stochastic effects of radiation are the result of mutations in the DNA molecule in cells. These cells retain the ability to divide and do not die through mitotic death. Over time, these mutations can accumulate and lead to the malignant transformation of cells and thus the development of cancer. These events are random, and the probability of mutations increases with the received dose. In any case, this dose must be low enough not to kill the cells. In principle, there is no dose so low that it could not potentially cause mutations. Therefore, the relationship between the probability of mutation occurrence and the dose of radiation is linear (see figure 23). The consequences of mutations are malignant cell transformations, which means that this effect is not dependent on the dose of radiation; only the probability of the effect’s occurrence is dose-dependent. As the received dose of radiation increases, the probability of stochastic effects also increases.

It is also characteristic of stochastic effects that they occur with a significant time delay; for example, the interval until the appearance of blood cancers is about seven years and for solid tumors about ten years. When a mutation occurs in germ cells, this mutation is passed on to offspring, and in this case, we refer to it as hereditary radiation effects. row.Question:
16. What is the principal purpose of tumor lysis syndrome prophylaxis in hematologic malignancies?
a. Prevent venous thromboembolism
b. Prevent infection from neutropenia
c. Prevent metabolic complications from rapid cell lysis
d. Prevent mucositis
e. Prevent cardiotoxicity
row.Text Answer: Prevent metabolic complications from rapid cell lysis
row.Reference: Strojan, P., & Hočevar, M. (Eds.). (2018). Onkologija: Učbenik za študente medicine [Oncology: Textbook for medical students] (1st ed.). Onkološki inštitut Ljubljana.
row.Context: Tumor lysis syndrome or rapid tumor cell breakdown syndrome can cause severe metabolic disturbances. It arises from the accelerated breakdown of tumor cells and the release of intracellular contents into the bloodstream. It most commonly occurs at the start of treatment for rapidly growing and chemotherapy-sensitive cancers, such as acute leukemias and highly malignant lymphomas, especially Burkitt lymphoma; it is rare in solid tumors.

row.Question:
17. What is the most common site of distant metastasis for breast cancer?
a. Brain
b. Liver
c. Kidney
d. Skin
e. Bone
row.Reference: Strojan, P., & Hočevar, M. (Eds.). (2018). Onkologija: Učbenik za študente medicine [Oncology: Textbook for medical students] (1st ed.). Onkološki inštitut Ljubljana.
row.Context:
Invasive cancers are characterized by local growth and the ability to metastasize.
Breast cancer spreads via the lymphatic system to regional lymph nodes (axillary, internal mammary, and supraclavicular nodes). Hematogenous spread most commonly occurs to the lungs, liver, bones, and brain.
The clinical presentation depends on the size of the primary tumor, lymph node involvement, invasion into surrounding structures, and metastases in distant organs.

BONE MARROW SUPPRESSION
The action of cytostatics on rapidly dividing bone marrow cells results in bone marrow suppression (myelosuppression). Bone marrow suppression occurs in 80 to 100 percent of all patients treated with chemotherapy. The suppression of blood cell maturation is evident in the peripheral blood as leukopenia or neutropenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia. The maturation of all types of blood cells in the bone marrow can be affected, but neutropenia is the most common during treatment with standard doses of cytostatics. Bone marrow suppression usually occurs 7 to 14 days after chemotherapy, but with some cytostatics (carmustine, lomustine, melphalan) it is most pronounced later—between the 28th and 35th day after starting treatment.

If the nature of the incidentaloma cannot be conclusively determined and it has no clear hormonal activity, a contrast‐enhanced adrenal CT protocol can be performed. row.Text Answer: A genetic disease, more common in males, associated with a high risk of sudden cardiac death
row.Reference: Interna medicina (6. izd., str. XXXVIII, 1693). (2022). Medicinska fakulteta; Buča.
row.Context:
Sindrom Brugada je genetska bolezen, pri kateri je značilen nenormalen elektrokardiogram in povečano tveganje za nenadno srčno smrt.
Sindrom opredelimo z značilno elektrokardiografsko sliko pri osebah s strukturno normalnim srcem, sinkopo ali srčnim zastojem.
Pri mladih zdravih moških iz jugovzhodne Azije je sindrom Brugada pogost vzrok nenadne smrti zaradi prekatne fibrilacije. Smrt nastopi praviloma ponoči, med spanjem.

English:
Brugada syndrome is a genetic disorder characterized by an abnormal electrocardiogram and an increased risk of sudden cardiac death.
The syndrome is diagnosed by its distinctive ECG pattern in individuals with structurally normal hearts, presenting with syncope or cardiac arrest.
In young healthy men from Southeast Asia, Brugada syndrome is a common cause of sudden death due to ventricular fibrillation. Death typically occurs at night during sleep.

row.Reference: Interna medicina (6. izd., str. XXXVIII, 1693). (2022). Medicinska fakulteta; Buča.
row.Context: Klinična slika. Pri akutni disekciji aorte je v ospredju hitro nastala, huda, ostra ali trgajoča bolečina v prsnem košu, ki seva pogosto v hrbet. Bolečina je stalna, lahko se s časom seli po arterah navzdol. Pri kronični disekciji ni bolečine. Kadar zapre disekcija vejo aorte, lahko povzroči srčni infarkt, obsežno možgansko kap, ishemijo katere koli okončine, ledvic, ishemijo mezenterikalnega področja z gangreno črevesja ali pa prekine vertebralne arterije s paraplegijo. Ob bolečini ima večina bolnikov povišan krvni tlak, če pa izmerimo nizek tlak, gre lahko za meritev na okončini z oslabljeno prekrvavitvijo zaradi disekcije (psevdohipotenzija), rupturo aorte, tamponado srca ali pa akutno insuficienco aortne zaklopke. Pri tamponadi srca so prekomerno napete vratne vene, pri akutni aortni insuficienci slišimo protomezodiastolični šum nad aortno zaklopko. Ob disekciji lahko nastane plevralni izlivi, navadno levorostranski, ki je lahko posledica vnetne reakcije ali pa krvavitve v plevralni prostor. Redko pride zaradi pritiska na nervus recurrens do hripavosti in Hornerjevega sindroma. English: Clinical presentation. In acute aortic dissection, the hallmark is a sudden onset of severe, sharp or tearing chest pain that often radiates to the back. The pain is constant and may migrate downward along the arterial tree over time. In chronic dissection, pain is absent. If the dissection occludes an aortic branch, it can result in myocardial infarction, a major stroke, ischemia of any extremity, renal ischemia, mesenteric ischemia with bowel gangrene, or vertebral artery obstruction leading to paraplegia. Most patients are hypertensive at the time of pain, but if hypotension is measured, it may be due to measuring on a limb with compromised perfusion from the dissection (pseudohypotension), aortic rupture, cardiac tamponade, or acute aortic valve insufficiency. In tamponade, the jugular veins are markedly distended; in acute aortic insufficiency, a protodiastolic murmur is heard over the aortic valve. Dissection may also lead to pleural effusions—typically left‐sided—owing to inflammation or bleeding into the pleural space. Rarely, compression of the recurrent laryngeal nerve causes hoarseness or a Horner’s syndrome.
